questions.question: A CRITICAL proximity alert appears. What is the first thing to do?
options: Acknowledge the alert and keep working
Stop movement and hold the controls in neutral
Reverse away quickly
Swing the upper structure to look around
questions.explanation: Stop first, then find the person or object. Moving quickly may bring the machine closer to someone you cannot see.

questions.question: Which area is a major blind spot on an excavator?
options: The bucket teeth when the bucket is on the ground
The area directly in front of the cab window
The rear counterweight and the side opposite the boom
The top of the cab
questions.explanation: The counterweight and the far side of the boom are hard to see from the seat.

questions.question: You lose sight of your spotter. What should you do?
options: Continue with the last signal given
Stop immediately
Sound the horn and keep going
Speed up to finish the move
questions.explanation: Stop as soon as you cannot see the spotter. Their signals are only useful while you can see them.

questions.question: Whose stop signal must you follow?
options: Only the assigned spotter
Only the site supervisor
Anyone who gives it
Nobody while the alert is active
questions.explanation: Follow a stop signal from anyone. Other signals come only from the assigned spotter.

questions.question: Why is the swing radius dangerous?
options: It raises engine temperature
A person inside it can be struck or pinned when the upper structure turns
It reduces bucket capacity
It only matters when travelling
questions.explanation: The rear of the machine sweeps a circle when rotating. Keep that area clear or barricaded.
